name: No-overclaim firewall and evidence separation
question: Are narrow evidence types prevented from claiming full runtime, quality, learnability, semantic readiness, common readiness, target promotion, rollback safety, or final extension functionality?
finding_before: Section 11 listed forbidden claims but did not require a report-level evidence separation matrix.
Reports could still overclaim dashboard/API, handler-level, test-only, static JSON, smoke, positive-only, token, quality, DPO, local-training, fresh-load, held-out, ablation, or rollback evidence.
Reports did not have mandatory user-visible wording for what the evidence proves, what it does not prove, and what independent track continues without a stop gate.
recheck_evidence: Plan now requires each report to state narrow proof scope, forbidden overclaims, user-visible limitation wording, and the next independent approved track so missing evidence does not become either a false stop gate or a false readiness claim.
